question.problem:
$\,$ $5$ is integer or $5$ is positive.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(5\text{ is integer}\text{ or }5\text{ is positive}) & ≡¬((5\text{ is integer})∨(5\text{ is positive})) \\  & ≡¬(5\text{ is integer})∧¬(5\text{ is positive}) \\  & ≡(5\text{ is not integer})∧(5\text{ is not positive}) \\  & ≡5\text{ is not integer}\text{ and }5\text{ is not positive}.\end{aligned}
$$
